title: Plans and the future
intro: Dutch often talks about the future with the normal present tense and a time word. For plans, add gaan. For promises, offers and guesses, use zullen.

notes.title: 1. Present tense plus a time word
body: The easiest way to talk about the future is the present tense. A word like morgen, straks, volgende week or zaterdag tells the listener it is the future.
Remember verb second. If you start with the time word, the subject comes after the verb.

examples.en: Spin class starts again next week.

notes.title: 2. Plans: gaan + a verb at the end
body: For plans, put a form of gaan in second place and the main verb at the very end. It works like English “going to”.
Gaan on its own still means going somewhere: ik ga naar de sportschool.

examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 11: Verbs in final position

notes.title: 3. zullen: promises and guesses
body: Zullen is the formal future: ik zal, jij zal or zult, hij zal, wij zullen. The main verb goes to the end.
When people talk, you hear it mostly in promises and guesses. Ik zal het doen means “I'll do it, I promise.” Dat zal wel lukken means “That will probably work out.”

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 9: Future with zullen

notes.title: 4. Offers and ideas: Zal ik…? Zullen we…?
body: Zal ik…? offers to do something, like “Shall I…?”. Zullen we…? suggests doing something together, like “Shall we…?” or “Let's…”.

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 9: zullen and other helping verbs

notes.title: 5. Towards A2: van plan zijn om … te …
body: To say what you intend to do, use van plan zijn om … te …, with te and the verb at the very end. Zin hebben om … te … works the same way and means “feel like”.
With a split verb, te goes between the two parts: mee te gaan, op te staan.

examples.nl: Ik ben van plan om een halve marathon [te lopen].
examples.en: I'm planning to run a half marathon.

examples.nl: Heb je zin om [mee te gaan]?
examples.en: Do you feel like coming along?

examples.nl: Ik ben van plan om vroeg [op te staan].
examples.en: I'm planning to get up early.

cards.rule: Present tense plus morgen. Start with morgen and the verb still comes second.
Present tense plus straks.

cards.nl: Volgende week begint de spinningles weer.
cards.en: Spin class starts again next week.
alts: De spinningles begint volgende week weer.
cards.rule: Present tense plus volgende week.

cards.en: What time will you be home?
cards.rule: Present tense: the context shows it is the future.
ga second, hardlopen at the end in one piece.

cards.nl: Wat ga je dit weekend doen?
cards.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

reply.nl: We gaan naar opa en oma.
reply.en: We're going to Grandma and Grandpa's.

cards.rule: Question word, ga, then doen at the end.
gaan second, eten at the end.

cards.en: I'm going to buy new strings.
cards.rule: gaan second, kopen at the end.
A promise: zal second, meenemen at the end.
A guess: zal … wel.
A guess: zal … wel, with zijn at the end.

cards.nl: Ik zal je een bericht sturen.
cards.rule: A promise: zal second, sturen at the end.
An offer: Zal ik…?
An idea for both of you: Zullen we…?

cards.nl: Zullen we om zeven uur afspreken?
cards.rule: Zullen we…? with afspreken at the end.

cards.en: Shall I pick up the kids?

reply.en: Yes please, that would be great.

cards.rule: An offer: Zal ik…? with ophalen at the end in one piece.

cards.nl: Ik ben van plan om een halve marathon te lopen.
cards.en: I'm planning to run a half marathon.
cards.rule: van plan zijn om … te lopen.

cards.nl: Heb je zin om mee te gaan?
cards.en: Do you feel like coming along?
cards.rule: zin om … te: meegaan becomes mee te gaan.

cards.nl: Ik ben van plan om vroeg op te staan.
cards.en: I'm planning to get up early.
cards.rule: opstaan with te in the middle: op te staan.

cards.nl: Ik wil volgend jaar een marathon lopen.
cards.en: I want to run a marathon next year.
alts: Volgend jaar wil ik een marathon lopen.
cards.rule: wil second, lopen at the end.
